nameStory: This moss gets its name from the rough, bumpy texture of its main stems when you run your finger along them. The 'feather-moss' part comes from the way its branches spread out in delicate, feathery patterns that remind you of tiny green plumes.
description: Rough-stalked Feather-moss is a common woodland moss that forms loose, sprawling mats across the forest floor. It grows in bright to yellow-green patches that can spread several feet wide, with individual stems reaching 2-4 inches long. The moss has a distinctive feathery appearance with irregularly branched stems that create an almost fern-like pattern when viewed from above.

idTips.label: Growth Form
idTips.description: Forms loose, spreading mats rather than tight cushions, with stems that branch irregularly in a feathery pattern

idTips.label: Texture
idTips.description: Main stems feel noticeably rough and bumpy when you gently rub them between your fingers, unlike smoother moss species

idTips.label: Leaves
idTips.description: Tiny oval leaves overlap like shingles along the stem, each with a sharp point and visible central vein when viewed with a hand lens

idTips.label: Color
idTips.description: Bright green when moist, becoming yellowish or golden-green when dry, with stems often showing reddish-brown coloration

idTips.label: Sporophytes
idTips.description: Curved capsules on reddish stalks appear spring through fall, often tilted at an angle rather than standing straight up

idTips.label: Habitat
idTips.description: Typically found on soil, rotting logs, and tree bases in shaded to partially sunny locations

habitat: Look for this adaptable moss in deciduous and mixed forests throughout New England, where it thrives on rich soil, decaying logs, and at the base of trees. It prefers partially shaded areas but can tolerate more sunlight than many forest mosses. You'll often find it mixed with other mosses and small ferns in woodland gardens and along forest paths.

seasonality.spring: Becomes vibrant green as moisture returns, with new sporophyte capsules beginning to develop on curved stalks.
seasonality.summer: Maintains bright green color in shaded areas but may appear more golden in drier spots. Sporophytes mature and release spores.
seasonality.fall: Often shows its most golden coloration as humidity drops, though it remains visible and identifiable.
seasonality.winter: Persists under snow cover, becoming darker green and more compressed but still recognizable by its rough stem texture.

funFact: This moss can actually help predict air quality — it's sensitive to pollution and tends to disappear from areas with heavy air contamination, making it a natural environmental monitor that scientists use to assess ecosystem health.
confusionNotes: Most easily confused with Smooth-stalk Feather-moss, but a simple finger test along the main stem will reveal the key difference — rough stems versus smooth ones. Remember: 'rough name, rough feel' for this species.
contextualKnowledge: Despite being called 'rough-stalked,' this moss is perfectly safe to touch and examine. The roughness refers to tiny bumps on the stem surface, not sharp or harmful textures.
compareHints: Among its feather-moss relatives, Rough-stalked Feather-moss stands out for its bumpy stem texture — Smooth-stalk Feather-moss feels smooth, Waterside Feather-moss prefers wet areas, and Whitish Feather-moss has a distinctly paler, more silvery appearance. The rough stems are your best clue for positive identification.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Unlike its relatives Smooth-stalk and Rough-stalked Feather-moss which can tolerate drier conditions, Waterside Feather Moss is strictly aquatic in its needs.

Among its Brachythecium relatives, Smooth-stalk Feather-moss is the most generalist - while Waterside Feather Moss prefers wet areas and Whitish Feather-moss has a distinctly paler color, this species grows almost anywhere.
Compared to its Brachythecium relatives like Rough-stalked and Smooth-stalk Feather-moss, Whitish Feather-moss is distinctly paler in color and typically smaller in overall size.

Unlike its relatives Waterside Feather Moss (which prefers wet areas) and Smooth-stalk Feather-moss (which forms denser mats), Pleated Foxtail Moss has those distinctive pleated leaves and prefers drier, more disturbed habitats.
